C482 No.1184 of 2022  Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Bhupesh Kandpal, Advocate, for the applicants.
Mr. V.K. Gemini, DAG, for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Karan Anand, Advocate, for the respondent No.2.
It is rather the conduct of the applicant no.2, which has called upon the Court to pass this order.

Primarily, the history of the litigation was emanated from the Criminal Case No.5614 of 2021, "State Vs. Samrat Bhandula and others", being the proceedings, which has been drawn against them for trying them for the offences under sections 498A, 323, 504 and 506 of IPC, and under sections  of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

sentences.text: After the initiation of the aforesaid proceedings, the criminal case was put to motion by submission of the Chargesheet No.140 of 2021, dated 15.04.2021.

Consequent to which, the summoning order was issued against the present applicants for being tried for the offences as aforesaid in Criminal Case No.5614 of 2021, "State Vs. Samrat Bhandula and others".

sentences.text: The matter was heard initially, and considering the fact that the parties were under a matrimonial litigation, coupled with the fact that considering the aspect, that out of the matrimony, there is a girl child, whose interest is also to be taken care of, this Court made an effort for calling upon the parties to enter into a mediation.

Consequently, in compliance of the order dated 25.08.2023, the parties did appear on the date fixed, and after interacting with them in the Chamber, this Court has settled the dispute by an order dated 29.08.2023.

As a consequence thereto, the Court expected that the parties would be settling their scores and will be rejoining themselves to discharge their matrimonial obligations, but the same was not accepted by the applicants and instead of reuniting themselves, the applicants has apparently shown their disinterest to continue with the matrimonial obligation.

Consequently, the respondent No.2, had to file a recall application on 01.10.2023, contending thereof, that there has been an apparent dereliction on part of the applicants to comply the order, which was rendered by this Court,
ultimately on 29.08.2023.

In the application, thus, preferred, the factum of death of one of the relatives of the applicants was also brought on record, which was submitted, that it might have been a consequence of, to be giving a reason to not to comply with the order passed by this Court earlier because of the sad demise,
which has taken place in the family of the applicants, but that in itself cannot be a reason to, not to adhere to the terms and conditions of the order dated 29.08.2023.
When the recall application was taken up on the previous occasion, the learned counsel for the applicants had vehemently opposed the recall application, and has sought time to file objection to it,
which has not been filed till date, and rather when the matter was taken up today, learned counsel for the applicants has made a statement that he has filed a reply in the Registry.
It might be a clever device to delay the proceedings to consider the recall application, when the same was not filed within time granted by this Court.

There are various facets, which has been argued by the learned counsel for the applicants for his inability to comply with the order dated 29.08.2023, are owing to the sad demise, which has taken place in the family, but the same cannot be an exclusive reason, rather it reflects the mental intellect of the applicants, and a clever device adopted by him to avoid compliance of the order, which was amicably settled between them in the chambers, on the pretext of the sad demise of the family member, but on the contrary on the basis of the settlement arrived at between the parties, all the cases trusting the undertaking given by the applicants before this Court for rejoining the family had been withdrawn on the application of applicant number 2.

It is on the pretext of the order passed by this Court on 29.08.2023, on one hand the applicants have taken a ground as argued by the learned counsel for the applicants that he could put an appearance because of the sad demise of late Mr. Chandra Kumar, but on the other hand he himself is an applicant to the proceedings before the learned trial court for seeking its closure on the ground of the order passed by this Court on 29.08.2023.
In fact it is not only the betrayal of the complainant/respondent no.2, but it is rather a betrayal on part of the applicants against the court itself by derilicting to comply the order.
Since all the proceedings have been withdrawn on the application preferred by the applicants in fact nothing survives on merits to be decided in this C482 application, but since it was a clever conspiracy which was hatched by the applicants of getting all the proceedings withdrawn, this C482 application is dismissed with the liberty left open for the respondent no.2/complainant, to resort to any proceedings by registering a criminal complaint against the present applicants as permissible in It Is Rather The Conduct Of The vs As A Consequence Thereto on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41623725/
2 accordance with law.

In fact, this Court was inclined to take a suo motu contempt action against the present applicants for misleading the court itself, but that too itself would be an issue open for the complainant, to be agitated before the trial court on registering of the complaint.

On account of the atrocious act of the applicants, they have imposed with the cost of Rs.50,000/-, to be deposited into the accounts of the daughter, who is the main sufferer because of the litigation.
The Registrar General of this Court, is hereby directed to register an FIR against the present applicants, for perjury and for intentional betrayal of the order passed by this Court.
Subject to the aforesaid, this C482 application is dismissed.

(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.) 17.10.2023 NR It Is Rather The Conduct Of The vs As A Consequence Thereto on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41623725/
